title: Hello, World!
objective: Use print() and string literals to produce exact text output.

sourceAlignment.title: Python Crash Course, 3rd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Eric Matthes
sourceAlignment.note: Adapted for Code Forge's in-browser Pyodide runtime — no local installation. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: print() is a function: a named, reusable action. You call it by writing its name followed by parentheses, and you hand it the thing you want it to display by placing that value inside the parentheses.

Text values in Python are called strings, and you write them surrounded by quotes — either single quotes or double quotes both work, as long as the opening and closing quote match. Anything inside the quotes is printed exactly as written, including spaces and punctuation.

Programmers traditionally write a tiny program that prints Hello, World! as the first thing they run in a new language. It confirms two things at once: the interpreter works, and you know how to produce output.
explanation.rule: print("some text") outputs the exact text inside the quotes, followed by a new line.

examples.title: Two Ways to Quote
examples.note: Single and double quotes both create the same kind of string. Pick one style and be consistent.

checks.question: Which of these is a valid Python string?

feedback.correct: Correct — the opening and closing quotes match.
feedback.incorrect: A string's opening and closing quote characters must match.

assignment.title: Hello, Forge!
assignment.brief: Write greet_forge() that prints exactly: Hello, Forge!
requirements: Use print() exactly once inside the function.
The printed text must be exactly: Hello, Forge!
assignment.starterCode:
def greet_forge():
    # Print the greeting here.
    pass

greet_forge()
assignment.testHarness:
# ---- Code Forge validation ----
import io, contextlib
_cf_buf = io.StringIO()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(_cf_buf):
    greet_forge()
_cf_result = _cf_buf.getvalue()
print("__CF_TEST_OUTPUT__")
print(repr(_cf_result))

hints: Use print() with a string inside the parentheses.
The comma and exclamation point are part of the required text.
Single or double quotes both work, just make the opening and closing quote match.
Capitalization matters: Hello and Forge both start with a capital letter.
